# R749SPL — exact Walsh zero-gap diagonal bridge and continuous BRC centers

**Date:** 2026-11-15. **Scientific status:** AUTHOR_EXACT_NOT_REVIEWED. **Frozen scientific input:** awdawmip/enterprise-math@a72226e2430ffa4786321ac86e7f0c599d5f0389. **Immediate predecessor:** R749SPK at 966fff21517fa62032636f9dc2598cc02f94fa61, Draft PR #2443.

This is an independently executable theorem in the frozen auxiliary sixteen-atom compatible Walsh source model. The four-branch BRC variables retain all Walsh coefficients and source identities. The theorem does not assume an X6/V29/V39 transfer.

## 1. Complete model and the new domain

For k in F_2^4, let χ_m(k)=(-1)^{popcount(k&m)}. For real parameters define the sixteen probabilities

\[
p_{t,s,h,u,v,w,z}(k)=\frac{1+t\chi_3(k)+s\chi_{12}(k)+h\chi_{15}(k)+u\chi_1(k)+v\chi_2(k)+w\chi_4(k)+z\chi_8(k)}{16}.
\]

Let F(t,s) be the set of all nonnegative laws of this form for given t,s. Let TV(P,Q)=\frac12\sum_k|P(k)-Q(k)|, let ρ(t,s)=\min_{q\in\Delta_{15}}\sup_{P\in F(t,s)}TV(P,q), and let ρcal(t,s)=\min_{q\in F(t,s)}\sup_{P\in F(t,s)}TV(P,q). Define g=ρcal−ρ.

Consider the closed triangle

\[
Q=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(1/5,1/5),(1/5,2/5)\}
=\{0\le t\le1/5,\quad t\le s\le2t\}.
\]

**Theorem R749SPL (every real t,s in Q):**

\[
\boxed{\rho(t,s)=\rho_{\mathrm{cal}}(t,s)=\frac{1-t}{2},\qquad g(t,s)=0.}
\]

An explicit optimal compatible center is

\[
\boxed{q_{t,s}=p_{t,s,\,2t-s,\,0,0,0,0}.}
\]

Swapping the two Walsh bit pairs proves the reflected theorem on
Qτ=conv{(0,0),(1/5,1/5),(2/5,1/5)}, with common radius (1−s)/2 and center p_{t,s,\,2s-t,0,0,0,0}.

Each newly proved triangle has area 1/50. Together they contribute 1/25 of new zero-gap parameter area, meeting the earlier two R749SPK wedges only on their edges. Their combined **proved lower-parameter zero-gap union has area 6/25** (R749SPK 1/5 plus R749SPL 1/25).

## 2. Same-fiber diameter lower bound

The R749SPK predecessor supplies, for all t,s≥0 and t+s≤1, explicit complete compatible laws

\[
P_\pm=p_{t,s,0,-t,-t,\ \pm s,\ \pm(1-t)}.
\]

Write a=χ_3, b=χ_12, c=χ_1, d=χ_4 and
16p_{abcd}=M_{ab}+cU_a+dV_b, where M_{ab}=1+at+bs+abh, U_a=u+av, and V_b=w+bz.

For P± one has h=0, U_+=−2t, U_−=0 and |V_+|=1−t+s, |V_−|=1−t−s. On t+s≤1 all four source-positivity inequalities M_{ab}≥|U_a|+|V_b| hold (in fact as equalities). The two laws are in the *same* F(t,s), with

\[
TV(P_+,P_-)=1-t.
\]

Thus every unrestricted probability center has maximal risk ≥(1−t)/2, proving ρ≥(1−t)/2 on Q. This retains the complete signed sixteen-atom source identity of the witnesses.

## 3. Compatible center and reduced BRC upper certificate

For q=p_{t,s,2t-s,0,0,0,0}, the four BRC masses are
M++=1+3t; M+−=1−t; M−+=1−3t+2s; M−−=1+t−2s.
They are nonnegative at the three vertices of Q and hence everywhere on Q by affinity. Therefore q lies in the same fiber.

For any source law and each a,b, positivity is *exactly* M_{ab}≥|U_a|+|V_b|. Its TV distance from q is invariant under independent changes of the four signs of U_+, U_−, V_+, V_−. This sign normalization is valid for this exact TV observer and this one-step risk, because all c,d∈{±1} appear within each block. It does not erase the original source labels in the underlying model. Thus set X=|U_+|, Y=|U_-|, Z=|V_+|, W=|V_-|, each ≥0.

The full joint parameter/source polytope has variables (t,s,h,X,Y,Z,W), bounded by the *twelve exact rational half-spaces*: four block-source inequalities, X,Y,Z,W≥0, t≥0, s−t≥0, 2t−s≥0, and 1−5t≥0.

For nonnegative A,B,C define the exact four-atom block mean

\[
\frac14\sum_{c,d=\pm1}|A+cB+dC|
=\max\left(A,B,C,\frac{A+B+C}{2}\right)=H(A,B,C).
\]

It follows for arbitrary feasible x that

\[
TV(p_x,q_{t,s})=
\frac18\sum_{a,b=\pm1}
H\left(|h-(2t-s)|,\ |U_a|,\ |V_b|\right).
\]

The right-hand side minus (1−t)/2 is convex in all seven joint variables: it equals an absolute-value norm of affine Walsh coefficients minus an affine target. The polytope is compact and has full dimension. Hence its maximum occurs at a vertex.

The attached self-contained Python certificate exhausts all C(12,7)=**792** candidate active-constraint bases by integer Bareiss elimination and exact Fraction back substitution, discards singular/infeasible sets, and deduplicates rational vertices. It returns:

| Exact metric | Result |
|---|---:|
| Candidate bases | 792 |
| Nonsingular bases | 361 |
| Feasible bases (including repetitions) | 154 |
| Distinct exact vertices | **47** |
| Vertices attaining the upper bound | 28 |
| Maximum risk excess over (1−t)/2 | **0** |
| Program result | **PASS** |

Vertex parameter projections: (0,0): 12; (1/5,1/5): 18; (1/5,2/5): 17. Every vertex was also checked using the **unreduced full sixteen-atom Walsh law**, including nonnegativity, normalization, equal TV values for original/reduced formula, the explicit lower-bound source pair and its exact distance. Every one of the 16 bit-pair permutation identities was checked. No floating-point tolerance is used in the theorem certificate.

Convexity extends the matching upper inequality to **all real** (t,s)∈Q and all full compatible laws, completing ρcal≤(1−t)/2. Together with Section 2 and ρ≤ρcal, this proves the theorem.

## 4. Gluing to the established R749SPK wedges

The earlier triangle T=conv{(0,0),(0,1),(1/5,2/5)} has common minimax center q0=p_{t,s,0,0,0,0,0}. Along the shared boundary s=2t the new center has h=2t−s=0, so the centers agree exactly. On the reflected seam t=2s they also agree. Along the diagonal s=t the two new reflected centers both have h=t=s, so a continuous compatible center selection exists across all four proved triangles.

The new zero-gap union may be viewed as two attached quadrilaterals, each of area 3/25, meeting on the diagonal segment from (0,0) to (1/5,1/5). This is a constructive continuation of the original R749SPK result rather than a claim about the full zero-gap boundary.

## 5. Reproduction, scope and next question

Run: python3 R749SPL_NEW_ZERO_GAP_BRIDGE_EXACT_CERT.py > R749SPL_NEW_ZERO_GAP_BRIDGE_RESULTS.json

Evidence: the accompanying script and saved complete PASS JSON. The full finite certificate proves the continuous-parameter upper bound by vertex completeness/convexity; independent review and formal Lean checking have not occurred. The theorem is internal to the declared auxiliary Walsh model. Frozen source: a72226e2430ffa4786321ac86e7f0c599d5f0389; predecessor: 966fff21517fa62032636f9dc2598cc02f94fa61.

**Next discriminating unit:** determine the actual free/calibrated radius phase for s=t just above t=1/5 (e.g. t=21/100), where the preceding simple centers become suboptimal; seek explicit source/event dual witnesses and an exact short interval theorem. A second direction is the exact zero/positive boundary adjacent to the new slanted edge s+3t=1. Source-preserving native X6/V29/V39 transfer remains a separate open bridge.
